title: Incremental fragment dispatcher for Python SDK + composable soft-fallback retry patterns
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers using streaming chat completions report opaque failures when intermittent network errors, proxies, or server-side partial responses occur. Current SDK primitives either force the user to re-run the entire request on failure (losing partial work) or expose a low-level bytes/coroutine surface that is hard to compose with application-level event handlers.

Goal: Provide a higher-level, ergonomic Python SDK abstraction that: (1) incrementally dispatches logically typed fragments (tokens, deltas, function-calls, metadata events) to user handlers, (2) composes with retry/backoff policies that can perform soft fallbacks (resume from last checkpoint or switch to polling fallback), and (3) emits structured telemetry for observability. The API should minimize ceremony for common patterns while remaining extensible for advanced use cases.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A new public Python class FragmentDispatcher with a minimal handler contract is implemented and documented.
2) Handlers receive typed events ("tokens", "chunk_end", "call_arg", "meta_error") and can acknowledge checkpoints. SDK supports checkpoint serialization so users can persist/restore progress.

3) Built-in RetryPolicy composition supports: exponential backoff, max-attempts, and soft-fallback strategy that will automatically attempt to resume via a resumable replay endpoint or switch to a non-streaming polling endpoint if resume fails.
4) End-to-end integration tests simulate network interruptions and assert correct handler invocation ordering, at-most-once token delivery when resume occurs, and final completion/error semantics.
5) Telemetry events emitted: sdk.streaming.fragment_received, sdk.streaming.checkpoint_saved, sdk.streaming.fallback_triggered, sdk.streaming.retry_attempt. Document sample dashboards.
6) Backwards-compatible: existing streaming API surface remains functional; new dispatcher introduced in an additive manner and gated behind an opt-in import path.
7) Example in docs: two idiomatic recipes (simple chat consumer and function-call-aware consumer) included in README with code snippets and tests.
8) Release notes and a migration guide for advanced users who want to adopt checkpoint persistence or custom fallback policies.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API design + two reference handler recipes; prototype local dispatcher that replays fragments from a mock stream (no network).
Week 2: Integrate RetryPolicy composators and soft-fallback manager; add checkpoint serialization helpers and small on-disk example using tempfile.
Week 3: End-to-end integration tests against staging streaming endpoint including flaky proxy simulation; update docs and examples.
Week 4: Iterate on ergonomics after design review, add telemetry hooks and gating config; prepare PR and run CI.
Rollout: feature-flagged release behind TOGGLE_PY_SDK_FRAGMENT_DISPATCHER for one week with opt-in telemetry collection.
api_proposal:
# Example API proposal (Python, illustrative)

class FragmentDispatcher:
    """Dispatches typed fragments from a streaming response to user handlers.

    Handlers: on_token(token:str), on_call_arg(name:str, value:str), on_event(name:str, payload:dict), on_complete(), on_error(exc: Exception)
    Supports: checkpoints(), resume(checkpoint_blob), and soft_fallback()
    """
    def __init__(self, transport, retry_policy=None, telemetry=None):
        self.transport = transport
        self.retry_policy = retry_policy or RetryPolicy.default()
        self.telemetry = telemetry

    async def run(self, handlers, checkpoint_store=None):
        "Run dispatcher. handlers is an object with async callbacks."
        last_checkpoint = None
        try:
            async for raw_frag in self.transport.stream():
                frag = self._parse(raw_frag)
                await self._dispatch_to_handlers(frag, handlers)
                if frag.is_checkpoint_candidate():
                    last_checkpoint = self._make_checkpoint(frag)
                    if checkpoint_store:
                        checkpoint_store.save(last_checkpoint)
                        self.telemetry.emit('sdk.streaming.checkpoint_saved', { 'checkpoint_size': len(last_checkpoint) })
        except TransientNetworkError as e:
            self.telemetry.emit('sdk.streaming.retry_attempt', { 'error': str(e) })
            if self.retry_policy.should_resume_from_checkpoint(last_checkpoint):
                resumed = await self._attempt_resume(last_checkpoint, handlers)
                if not resumed and self.retry_policy.should_fallback_to_polling():
                    self.telemetry.emit('sdk.streaming.fallback_triggered', { 'reason': 'resume_failed' })
                    await self._fallback_to_polling(handlers, last_checkpoint)
            else:
                raise

# Example handler usage
class SimpleChatHandlers:
    async def on_token(self, token):
        print(token, end='', flush=True)
    async def on_complete(self):
        print('
-- done --')

# Usage
# dispatcher = FragmentDispatcher(transport=HttpSseTransport(...))
# await dispatcher.run(SimpleChatHandlers())
tradeoffs: Designing for resumability increases the complexity of server-side contract (must provide resume token/endpoint). We implement resumable replay as best-effort: resume may drop or duplicate fragments in some edge cases; document guarantees (at-most-once token semantics only when server-side resume is exact).
Persisting checkpoints adds I/O overhead for high-throughput consumers; default policy will checkpoint infrequently (every N tokens or seconds) and allow opt-in aggressive checkpointing.
Soft-fallback to polling preserves availability but increases cost; make fallback opt-in per-app with clear telemetry and cost warnings.
We will not change existing low-level streaming primitives; dispatcher lives as an ergonomic layer that can be bypassed for advanced users.
